title: Document MCP search contract and supported query syntax
description:
Problem: public MemorySmith docs explain the purpose of the search tools and their basic arguments, but they do not clearly document the richer structured formats and query-syntax boundaries that external agents actually need. The runtime already supports `format=envelope` for REST and MCP retrieval surfaces, and `ChatToolCatalog` exposes `markdown`, `json`, and `envelope` for several search tools, but the operator-facing pages do not spell out when to use each format, what extra diagnostics/scores the envelope exposes, how Lucene-style lexical search differs from unsupported fielded or fuzzy-query assumptions, or how namespaced tags should be used in practice. This forces external agents to guess, then rediscover the contract by trial and error.

Evidence from 2026-05-26 audit:
- `MemorySmith.App/Controllers/MemoriesController.cs` and `MemorySmith.App/Controllers/PagesController.cs` implement `format=envelope`.
- `MemorySmith.App/Services/ChatToolCatalog.cs` advertises `markdown`, `json`, and `envelope` for relevant search tools.
- `README.md` and `Data/Pages/guides/search-and-chat.md` cover basic search modes, tool purpose, and permissions, but not the richer structured format guidance or supported lexical syntax boundaries.
- Search of `Data/Tasks` found no existing task that owns the public search-contract documentation gap.

Desired outcome: external agents and maintainers can use MemorySmith search tools correctly without probing undocumented formats or unsupported query patterns.

Scope:
- In scope: `README.md`, `Data/Pages/guides/search-and-chat.md`, `Data/Pages/features/api-and-mcp.md`, and related structured wiki updates that document search output formats and supported query syntax.
- In scope: examples for `markdown`, `json`, and `envelope`; notes about when score interpretation is meaningful; and clear guidance on namespaced tags and common lexical-query patterns.
- Out of scope: adding new search features such as date filters, pagination, or page semantic ranking.

Acceptance criteria:
- Public docs describe which search surfaces support `markdown`, `json`, and `envelope`, and what each format is for.
- Public docs explain the supported lexical-query habits and call out notable unsupported assumptions that external agents are likely to try.
- Public docs give at least one concrete example using namespaced tags and one using structured envelope output.
- The updated docs are linked from the main search/MCP guidance surfaces.

Validation:
- Run `./Scripts/Test-PageLinks.ps1` after doc changes.
- Run `./Scripts/Test-PagePathLiterals.ps1` after doc changes.
- Run `./Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1` after task creation/update.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created during Claude benchmark triage after verifying that the public docs cover permissions and basic search behavior but still omit the richer `envelope` guidance and practical lexical-syntax boundaries external agents are currently reverse-engineering.
